note: 25ª vaga (2026-08-28, Fase 24, continuação do R1). Tema: Emoções e estados psicológicos matizados. 15 headwords inicialmente escritos foram removidos por já existirem noutros bancos (envious/insecure/uneasy/devastated/heartbroken/nostalgic/indifferent/at ease/over the moon/embarrassed/jealous/ashamed/determined/get over/guilty) — verificado por comparação automática de todos os headwords do currículo antes do commit final.

words.definition_en: feeling reassured after anxiety or fear has ended
example_sentences: She was relieved when the test results came back normal.

words.definition_en: feeling annoyed because you cannot achieve what you want
example_sentences: He felt frustrated by the constant delays.

words.definition_en: having such strong feelings that you cannot think clearly
example_sentences: She was overwhelmed with gratitude.

words.definition_en: made to feel ashamed and foolish in front of others
example_sentences: He felt humiliated after being corrected in front of the team.

words.definition_en: feeling bitter about being treated unfairly
example_sentences: She grew resentful of always being overlooked for promotion.

words.definition_en: easily hurt emotionally or physically
example_sentences: Talking about it made her feel vulnerable.

words.definition_en: anxious about something that is about to happen
example_sentences: I was apprehensive about the interview.

words.definition_en: unable to relax or stay still because of anxiety or boredom
example_sentences: The children got restless during the long flight.

words.definition_en: in a state of peaceful satisfaction
example_sentences: She seems content with her new job.

words.definition_en: satisfied because you are achieving your potential
example_sentences: He feels fulfilled by his work as a teacher.

words.definition_en: feeling thankful
example_sentences: I'm grateful for all your help.

words.definition_en: feeling strong emotion, usually because of something touching
example_sentences: I was deeply moved by the speech.

words.definition_en: emotionally affected by something kind or sad
example_sentences: She was touched by their generosity.

words.definition_en: deep sorrow, especially caused by a death
example_sentences: He is still dealing with his grief.

words.definition_en: to feel deep sorrow, especially after a death
example_sentences: The whole town mourned the loss.

words.definition_en: a strong wish or desire for someone or something
example_sentences: She felt a deep longing for her hometown.

words.definition_en: causing both happiness and sadness at the same time
example_sentences: Graduation was a bittersweet moment for her.

words.definition_en: having mixed or contradictory feelings about something
example_sentences: He felt ambivalent about accepting the promotion.

words.definition_en: showing no interest, enthusiasm, or concern
example_sentences: Many voters felt apathetic about the election.

words.definition_en: disappointed after discovering something is not as good as believed
example_sentences: He became disillusioned with the company's promises.

words.definition_en: having doubts about whether something is true or will work
example_sentences: I'm skeptical that the plan will succeed.

words.definition_en: cautious about possible dangers or problems
example_sentences: She was wary of trusting him again.

words.definition_en: made to feel afraid or less confident by someone or something
example_sentences: He felt intimidated by her confidence.

words.definition_en: feeling discouraged by the size or difficulty of a task
example_sentences: She felt daunted by the scale of the project.

words.definition_en: having a strong reason to act or achieve something
example_sentences: She's very motivated to learn English.

words.definition_en: too satisfied with a situation, and unaware of possible problems
example_sentences: The team became complacent after their early success.

words.definition_en: able to recover quickly from difficulties
example_sentences: Children can be remarkably resilient.

words.definition_en: calm and in control of your emotions
example_sentences: She remained composed despite the pressure.

words.definition_en: feeling or appearing troubled or nervous
example_sentences: He became agitated when asked about the delay.

words.definition_en: easily annoyed
example_sentences: He gets irritable when he's tired.

words.definition_en: idiom: nervous, tense, or irritable
example_sentences: Everyone was on edge before the announcement.

words.definition_en: idiom: shocked or surprised by something unexpected
example_sentences: I was taken aback by his blunt response.

words.definition_en: idiom: feeling sad or depressed
example_sentences: He's been down in the dumps since losing the match.

words.definition_en: idiom: so worried or frustrated that you don't know what to do
example_sentences: After weeks of delays, she was at her wits' end.

words.definition_en: idiom: to stop yourself from saying something you want to say
example_sentences: I had to bite my tongue during the meeting.

words.definition_en: to speak suddenly and angrily
example_sentences: Sorry for snapping at you earlier — I was stressed.

words.definition_en: phrasal verb: to suddenly criticise or attack someone verbally
example_sentences: He lashed out at his colleagues after the criticism.

words.definition_en: phrasal verb: to suppress your feelings instead of expressing them
example_sentences: He tends to bottle up his emotions.

words.definition_en: to accept a difficult situation
example_sentences: He's still coming to terms with the loss.

words.definition_en: phrasal verb: to become more cheerful or energetic
example_sentences: She perked up after hearing the good news.

words.definition_en: phrasal verb: to become less angry, upset, or excited
example_sentences: Take a deep breath and calm down.

words.definition_en: phrasal verb: to become or make someone happier
example_sentences: I brought flowers to cheer her up.
